formNote: Mojidata IDS: ⿱𦍌我. The Shuowen: 義，己之威儀也, “one’s own dignified bearing”, from 我 and 羊. In later Chinese 義 also means “meaning”, as in 意義.
summary: Rightness: what one owes, and the bearing of a person who does it. Mencius put it next to humaneness, 仁義, and in Vietnam nhân nghĩa became a national ideal.
placement: On the left of the disk, opposite 智: rightness, facing discernment. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: The Sprout of Rightness
satellites.evidence: Mencius 2A6: 羞惡之心，義之端也 — “the heart of shame and aversion is the sprout of rightness.” One of the four sprouts, with humaneness, propriety and wisdom (see 仁 · 心).

satellites.title: Giving Up Life for What Is Right
satellites.evidence: Mencius 6A10: fish and bear’s paw cannot both be had; life and rightness cannot both be kept, 二者不可得兼，舍生而取義者也 — “give up life and take rightness”.
